newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Boeing gave in to European regulators' demands and won approval of its merger with McDonnell Douglas.
* Four large energy companies reported strong earnings.
* Trans World Airlines posted a bigger than expected loss.
* The Dow rose 26.71 points to close at a record 8,088.36.
* The dollar reached another six year high against the German mark.
* Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing said earnings rose 9.7 percent.
* Though Pennzoil, which once courted Union Pacific Resources, is now fighting off a hostile bid from that company, Union Pacific Resources now appears to be getting the upper hand in the struggle.
* Labor unrest continued at General Motors, as workers struck a plant in Warren, Mich.
* Eli Lilly reported a net loss.
* Jamie Tarses, the president of ABC Entertainment, said she was staying at the network, denying speculation that she was trying to get out of her contract or that ABC was trying to force her out.
* Production problems is most likely what led to the downfallof Maidenform Worldwide Inc, which filed for Chapter 11 protection Tuesday.
* Through his silence this week about the risks of a stock price bubble, Alan Greenspan may have been conceding that the market was right after all.
